Vitamin B12 deficiency is commonly associated with pernicious anemia, which is an autoimmune condition leading to chronic atrophic gastritis. This results in gastric mucosal atrophy, making atrophy the most expected morphological feature in a gastric biopsy. Intestinal metaplasia can occur due to chronic inflammation, but it is less directly linked to vitamin B12 deficiency than atrophy. Helicobacter pylori infection is a possible but not definitive finding in this context, as it is more commonly associated with chronic gastritis of other etiologies. Endocrine cell hyperplasia can occur in chronic gastritis but is not as directly linked to vitamin B12 deficiency as atrophy. Therefore, atrophy is the most consensus-supported morphological feature in this scenario.
